subject: history_social
passage: From 1819 to 1926, the princely state of Bhopal, in central India, was governed almost without interruption by women: a succession of four rulers known as the Begums of Bhopal. Historians have noted that several of these rulers invested heavily in public institutions, giving particular attention to education at a time when few states in the region did so. ______ Sultan Jahan Begum, who ruled from 1901 to 1926, established schools for girls in her state and, in 1920, became the first chancellor of Aligarh Muslim University.
stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

explanation.why: The second sentence makes a general claim about "several" of the Begums: they invested in education. The last sentence describes one of them, Sultan Jahan Begum, and her work for education. A transition that introduces one case of a general claim is needed.
explanation.A: Incorrect. "Specifically" would mean the sentence identifies exactly who the "several" rulers were, but it names only one of them. This is the closest near miss.
explanation.B: Correct. "For example" introduces Sultan Jahan Begum as one of the rulers who invested in education.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "Similarly" would introduce a separate case like one already described, but no individual ruler has been described before this sentence.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Her work supports the claim about the Begums' interest in education; it does not go against it.
